title: How to use the COUNTIF function
task: Count how many cells meet a condition — how many times a value appears, how many pass a threshold.

excel.note: COUNTIF(range, criteria). Comparisons and wildcards go in the quoted criteria.

explanation: COUNTIF takes just two things: the range to look through (A2:A5) and the criteria to count ("East") — here it finds "East" three times. The criteria is flexible: a number, exact text, a comparison in quotes (">100" counts values over 100), or wildcards ("E*" counts anything starting with E, "?at" matches cat/bat/hat). Two everyday uses: flag duplicates with =COUNTIF(range,cell)>1, and check membership with =COUNTIF(list,value)>0. For more than one condition use COUNTIFS, and to count blanks or non-blanks use COUNTBLANK or COUNTA.
